constraints: Preserve models, migrations, settings, URL configuration, templates, and deployment configuration while changing the Django release series.
Upgrade one feature release at a time, using the latest patch release of each series, as the Django upgrade guide recommends.
Confirm the target Django series supports the Python release in use and that third-party packages support both Django and Python.

steps.instructions: Change the reported Django pin or requirement from 3.1 to the next release series on the upgrade path, ending at a supported series such as 5.2 LTS, then regenerate lock files.
steps.title: Raise the Django requirement

steps.instructions: For each series crossed, read its release notes for backwards-incompatible changes and deprecations, resolve deprecation warnings, and update code that uses removed APIs.
steps.title: Apply the release notes

verification.purpose: Run Django's system checks against the upgraded project.
Run the project's test suite with deprecation warnings shown.
Confirm the installed distributions have no broken requirements.

rule.replacement: Django 5.2 LTS or a newer supported release
rule.summary: The Django project lists the 3.1 release series as unsupported: it no longer receives security updates or bug fixes, and its end of extended support was December 7, 2021.
rule.title: Django 3.1 is end-of-life
